reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound, as active-learning ML surrogates have been successfully used to accelerate free-energy calculations in elemental and binary systems, but the claim of capturing electron–vibration coupling and anharmonicity in liquids with only a modest training set is optimistic and lacks specific evidence for the proposed Ta-Cr/Ta-V systems.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and decisive, specifying a benchmark (Ta-Cr, Ta-V), a quantitative accuracy threshold (5% deviation), and a speed-up factor (10x vs. TOR-TILD), though it does not detail how the ML surrogate will be trained or how free energies will be extracted from it.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis directly addresses the research question by proposing a practical, testable method to reduce computational cost, and it would be highly valuable to researchers if validated, though it lacks concrete supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results as requested.
